notes: critic: unresolved after 2 replan(s): ['RQ1 on direct productivity effects relies entirely on one survey of UK academics (10.1007/s42438-023-00440-6) reporting perceived workload relief, not objective graduate student output metrics; no randomized trials or longitudinal studies measuring actual dissertation progress, pages drafted, or completion time exist, leaving this sub-question effectively unanswered despite passing count thresholds.', 'RQ2 on research quality and rigor in graduate research relies on hallucination rates from isolated tasks (reference generation in systematic reviews, legal research tools) and expert review of 4 AI-generated articles, but provides zero evidence of quality assessment in actual graduate dissertations or theses; the single undergraduate study linking tool reliance to performance (10.3390/app14104115, n=32, 10 weeks, programming only) does not generalize to graduate research contexts.', 'The conflict between performance improvement (10.1287/orsc.2023.18430, 10.1186/s41239-025-00526-0) and performance decline (10.3390/app14104115) is presented with a hypothesis but without sufficient evidence to distinguish when each pathway occurs in graduate research specifically; mechanisms operate in undergraduate programming (10 weeks), business problem-solving (crowdsourcing), and digital storytelling contexts, not graduate dissertation workflows.', 'RQ5 on academic integrity violations relies on hallucination rates and policy reviews rather than empirical audits of actual plagiarism, citation inaccuracies, or undetected violations in graduate student work; no measurement of integrity violation prevalence or correlation with AI use intensity exists among graduate students.']
